findings.finding: Counter-thesis (pre-mortem, a holder who bought at 405.83 on 2026-10-27 has lost money by 2029-10): the price (about 1.6T market cap, trailing GAAP P/E 446) needed robotaxi, FSD, Optimus and AI compute to become large, profitable businesses fast, and they did not. Meanwhile the core business stayed ex-growth. US and China revenue kept falling (Q3 2026 -14.4% and -7.9%; North American EV market -24% YTD), and the only growth was exports into BYD's markets. GAAP operating margin stayed at 2-5% (Q3 2026 2.6%, TTM 3.3%) because opex grew 39% on flat revenue and regulatory credits ran off (RPO 384M). About 20bn a year of capex went into compute, cells, Cybercab and Semi lines that earned below the cost of capital (TTM hand ROIC about 5%; incremental ROIC 2022-2025 negative). Paid robotaxi stayed small next to Waymo (about 500k paid rides a week in 11 cities), slowed by NHTSA probes, the Benavides verdict (329M, on appeal) and class actions. Energy margin fell back once the one-off Q3 IEEPA refunds (net about 447M, about 62% of Q3 operating income) ended and tariffs and OBBBA raised cell costs. Governance added to the losses: a SpaceX related-party deal under special-committee review (hypothesis) and the 2025 CEO award (423.7M shares, 105.8-120.4bn unrecognized cost if its milestones become probable). The market then re-rated the stock from narrative multiples toward an auto-and-energy multiple. What would have shown it early: Q4 2026 revenue below 26.6bn or Q1 2027 deliveries below 358k; FY2027 GAAP operating margin below 5%; no paid robotaxi on customer cars and no expansion beyond a few cities by mid-2027; Cybercab volume deliveries slipping past mid-2027; no EU-wide FSD approval by mid-2027; FY2027 capex at or above 20bn with free cash flow below 2bn or any draw on the 30bn credit lines; energy gross margin ex-refunds below 20% in Q4 2026 or Q1 2027. Counter to the engine's own reading: every scenario gives zero value to autonomy, Optimus and compute (core gaps). If customer-car robotaxi scales on the installed base (1.74M FSD subscriptions, +70% a year), the economics move outside all three driver sets, so the 38.9 fair value says 'the price is not explained by the reported business', not 'worth 38.9 with confidence'.
findings.where: position/core.json scenario_events.bear, key_risk, falsifiers; position/field.json thesis_he.bear; companies/TSLA/out/table_he.md
findings.fix: Show this counter-thesis (short form) next to the result. Add the early signals above as dated numeric falsifiers for the base and bull scenarios. State under the table that the model gives no value to robotaxi, FSD, Optimus or compute, so the gap to the price is the value of those options, which the model cannot measure.

findings.finding: What the price assumes. None of the scenarios has a path to today's price: the year-5 bull price is 201 (-51%) and the bull DCF value is 115.7. casefile val.what_must_be_true: no single lever reconciles the base case with 405.83. Growth over a -30% to +50% shift gives at most 38.9, a 39% mature margin gives 191.5, and capital efficiency gives at most 69.0. Only the discount rate solves, at 5.33%. My rerun of expectation_gap reconstructed the base anchor (NTM revenue 114.6bn, g1 9%, margin 3.3% to 9%, sales to capital 1.5, terminal ROIC 10.56%, cost of equity 8.561%, g 5%) and reproduced the engine within 3% (value 39.87 vs 38.90). With margin held at 9%, growth alone needs an 84.6% 5-year revenue CAGR, against a demonstrated 5.2% (FY2022 81.46bn to FY2025 94.83bn). Duration, margin (up to 70%) and capital efficiency are each not reachable alone. Red-team: casefile rk.redteam verdict passed, with no critical failures, but cash_reconciles, debt_complete and shares_current passed only 'by construction' (see the CEO-award shares finding).
findings.where: companies/TSLA/out/casefile.json val.what_must_be_true and rk.redteam; value.json summary; companies/TSLA/out/table_he.md
findings.fix: Say next to the result that the price implies a different business: about 80%+ revenue CAGR at a 9% margin, or the value of options that no scenario models. The bull is the engine's upside for the reported business, not a ceiling on the price. Keep the result a draft until the shares finding is fixed.

findings.finding: The path multiples sit below Tesla's whole own-history range, yet the base is shown as the most likely yearly price. The forward P/E in company_path runs 22.8 to 16.5 (base), 64.7 to 24.5 (bull) and 6.5 to 7.1 (bear). own_history (forward proxy, 2021-2025) is low 28.6, median 103.1, high 488.7; trailing is low 34.0 and now 446.0. As a result the table shows the base price at -91% within one year (37.5 in 2027/10). That requires a re-rating Tesla has never had, and no base event explains it. All three paths are labelled 'unproven', which is correct, but the table reads as a price forecast. The path's own gap also says the economics formula charges EPS recovery from today's depressed margin as reinvestment, so the bear and base multiples may be understated. The year-5 base path (56.1) is close to the DCF base at year 5 (53.3), which bounds that effect.
findings.where: value.json company_path.base/bear/bull; position/path.json company_path.own_history and gaps; companies/TSLA/out/table_he.md yearly table
findings.fix: Show the own-history multiple range (28.6/103.1/488.7) next to the yearly table. Label the yearly prices as fundamental values at an economics multiple, not the likely market price. State that reaching them needs the market to stop paying for the autonomy and robotics options.

findings.finding: Core and field tell different base stories. Core base growth_anchor +9% rests on car sales growing mid-single digits because 'demand is above production' (base event 1: backlog, 11 days of supply), with batteries as the limit. Field base says 'vehicle sales roughly flat and global share stable to slightly declining'. The evidence in the same parts (US -14.4%, China -7.9% in Q3, North American EV market -24%, Q3 revenue -0.2%) supports the field version. If autos are flat, base FY2027 growth is about 6%, not 9%: energy +20% on about 12.8bn, services and other +33%, credits to zero. The fair value depends on this driver only weakly, because growth at base ROIC near the cost of capital adds little value, but the base story is internally inconsistent.
findings.where: position/core.json drivers.growth_anchor.reason and scenario_events.base[0]; position/field.json thesis_he.base and potential.market_direction
findings.fix: Pick one base story. Either evidence the car-volume growth with production, deliveries and order numbers and align field, or set base growth_anchor to about 0.06 with autos flat and rerun ticker-value. The demand-above-production claim is management's opinion on the call: label it as such.

findings.finding: The bear does not break the margin; it raises it. Bear mature_margin 0.05 sits above the TTM 3.3% (casefile rk bear mechanism '3.3% -> 5.0%') and Q3 2026 2.6%. Bear EPS therefore rises from 1.09 to 1.40 over five years while revenue falls 3%. This contradicts the bear's own events: R&D and AI spending keep rising without revenue, margin 'stays 2-5%', credits vanish, and energy margin normalizes after the one-off refunds. The bear is FY2025 (4.6%) repeated, not a deterioration from today. The bear funding mechanism is also not in the numbers. Bear event 2 says the company 'needs the 30bn credit lines', but casefile rk.bear_levers shows financing modeled=false and debt constant at 9.267bn. The Q3 call guided no draws in 2026, while business.json flags that the 10-Q says heightened capex will need funding beyond operating cash flow.
findings.where: position/core.json drivers.mature_margin.bear and scenario_events.bear[1]; casefile rk.failure_scenarios[bear] and rk.bear_levers.financing; value.json company_path.bear
findings.fix: Set bear mature_margin at or below TTM (about 0.03), with sales_to_capital and ROIC consistent with it. Either size the funding gap (capex 20bn+ against operating cash flow, draws on the 30bn lines, interest) in the bear financing, or reword the event to 'may need' with that 10-Q passage as evidence. Then rerun ticker-value.

findings.finding: The DCF's terminal returns contradict the path's per-scenario returns. The core part left terminal_roic on engine rules, so the DCF uses 9.56% (bear), 10.56% (base) and 12.56% (bull). The path's evidenced ROICs are 6%, 12% and 20%. The field bear says ROIC stays below the cost of capital, but the bear DCF terminal ROIC of 9.56% is above the 8.561% cost of equity, so the bear terminal creates value. Terminal growth of 4.5-5% is close to the cost of equity and terminal share is 62%, so this moves the printed values. At 6% the bear reinvestment rate goes from 47% to 75% of NOPAT and the bear value falls well below 17.8. The bull at 20% would rise, the base at 12% rises about 6-7%. None of this changes the direction of the verdict.
findings.where: value.json company_path.economics.<s>.engine_terminal_roic; position/core.json gaps[2] (terminal_roic left on engine rules); position/path.json company_path.scenarios.<s>.roic; position/field.json thesis_he.bear
findings.fix: Set core terminal_roic per scenario to the path's evidenced ROICs (bear 0.06, base 0.12, bull 0.20), or give the reason for the difference. Rerun ticker-value so the fair value, buy-below price and bear/bull values come from one return story.

findings.finding: The 2025 CEO award is treated the same in every scenario. Opening shares are 3,952,757,946 (dc_shares_out_20261015, cover page, 'includes unvested restricted stock'). That count includes the 423,743,904 unearned award shares (dc_ceo_award_2025_shares), which the 10-Q excludes from diluted shares until earned. No engine scenario reaches the award's market-cap milestones (bull value 115.7 is about 0.46T), so in all three the shares would be forfeited. Every per-share value is therefore diluted by about 10.7%, while SBC is also charged at about 3.8% of revenue. My expectation_gap rerun gives a base anchor of 39.87 with 3.953bn shares and 44.66 with 3.529bn (+12%). In the bull, the award's operational milestones (FSD subscriptions, robotaxis, Optimus) could become probable, putting 105.8-120.4bn of unrecognized GAAP cost (dc_sbc_ceo_award_unrecognized_not_probable_low/high) into the GAAP EPS that company_path prices. That is not modeled. The red-team 'shares_current' check passed by construction only.
findings.where: companies/TSLA/out/casefile.json val.case.opening.shares and underwriting.opening_reconciliation.common_shares_outstanding; evidence_pack ids dc_shares_out_20261015, dc_ceo_award_2025_shares, dc_sbc_ceo_award_unrecognized_not_probable_low/high
findings.fix: Use about 3,529,014,042 economic shares, the point-in-time count less the unearned award, in the scenarios where the milestones are not met. Carry the award as scenario-conditional dilution (vesting only at its market-cap tranches). In the bull, state the GAAP EPS effect if operational milestones become probable. Rerun ticker-value.

findings.finding: The table row 'expected annual return at today's price about 5.3%' is a degenerate number, and it conflicts with the same table. The implied rate of 5.33% is only 0.33pp above the terminal growth of 5.0% (= risk-free), so it is almost entirely a near-perpetuity artifact (r close to g), not a return the owner can expect. The yearly table beside it shows the base at -86% over five years.
findings.where: companies/TSLA/out/table_he.md row 'תשואה שנתית צפויה במחיר של היום'; value.json summary.base_irr; casefile val.what_must_be_true[cost_of_equity]
findings.fix: When the implied rate is within about 1pp of terminal growth, show the row as 'not meaningful (the price implies a near-perpetual growth rate)', or show it together with the 5-year path return. Do not present 5.3% as the expected return.

findings.finding: The falsifiers would not refute their scenarios. The bull has one falsifier, on a minor line (FSD subscriptions below 2.0M at 2027-03-31). None tests the bull's own mechanisms: Cybercab customer deliveries by end-2026, customer cars in paid robotaxi around Q2 2027, EU-wide FSD approval, deliveries toward 2.25M capacity, Megapack toward 110 GWh. The bear falsifier fx_q2_rev_bear (Q2 2027 revenue above 31.0bn) needs +9.8% on Q2 2026 (28.236bn, pf_revenue_q_2026_06_30), i.e. base-level growth, so anything from -3% to +9.8% leaves the -3% bear standing. The base falsifier fx_q4_rev fires below 24.9bn (= Q4 2025, pf_revenue_q_2025_12_31), while the engine's own base implies Q4 2026 of about 28.0bn (FY2026 106.68bn less nine-month 78.67bn): it fires only about 11% below base. fx_fy27_margin below 3% sits 1.8pp under the base FY2027 margin of 4.8%.
findings.fix: Add dated numeric bull falsifiers: no paid robotaxi rides in customer-owned cars by 2027-06-30; Cybercab cumulative deliveries below a stated number by 2027-06-30; no EU-wide FSD approval by 2027-06-30; FY2027 storage deployed below a stated GWh. Tighten the bear to Q2 2027 revenue above about 29.1bn (+3%), the base Q4 2026 revenue to below about 26.6bn, and the FY2027 margin to below about 4%.

findings.finding: Evidenced flags are missing from the bear and the risks. findings.finding: The cost of equity used for the fair value (8.561%) is below the market's own 9.2% (risk-free 5.0% + ERP 4.2%), through risk_adjustment -0.0064 and net country risk -0.14%, for a company the engine itself rates quality 'weak' and risk 'high'. The direction raises every value, so it is conservative for the 'not cheap' reading and does not flip it.
